verdicts.reason: The user sits at CLIENT01 under the caption 'Secure RDP connection'. The target rdp01.1sn0s.lab is labelled by its FQDN. Nothing is trusted yet.
An amber pulse runs along the floor channel from the client to the RDP server. Amber means pending, and the channel is a network conduit, not a trust link.
The listener on rdp01.1sn0s.lab lights up. The server, not the client, is where the identity sits (F-01).
A pale card tagged 'Self-signed' is presented, and the client shows 'Unverified'. The channel stays amber, then the amber dies out of the channel, so the attempt ends (F-02, PKI-S0R1-01).
The RDPAuth badge drops from the AD/policy side onto rdp01. No client connection is pending, and no key or certificate comes from AD.
A key pair forms inside the RDP chassis. The private key (lock-motif head) and the public key (ring head) have distinct shapes. Caption: 'The private key stays on the server'.
The private key settles into the locked container and the lid closes. The public key stays outside.
The public key merges into the white capsule while the container stays closed. Caption: 'The request is signed, not the key sent'.
A beam from the glowing container seals the capsule with a band. No key-shaped object moves (F-04, F-03).

The capsule is held near the server, framed with 1SN0S.LAB, and a cyan route lights toward Issuing CA 1. The steel-blue query pulse is hard to see, and the capsule's position in f0765 is ambiguous (see K2-11), but nothing shows the request entering AD.

The RDP request capsule leaves the lit route to Issuing CA 1. It floats past the 1SN0S Root CA label (f0840) and lands on the Root CA's press on its gold plinth (f0867). An end-entity request reaches the offline root, a CA that publishes no templates. This contradicts AR-02, AR-01, F-05 and the model event E-04.2a (to: ISSUING_CA1).

The beat opens on the capsule sitting on the Root CA's press under the caption 'Issuing CA 1 verifies, then signs' (f0874). It then cuts inside Issuing CA 1, where the four checks resolve with no request present (f0930, f0987). The CA is evaluating a request that is not there, while the request sits at the root.

Issuing CA 1's press is never shown consuming a capsule or stamping a card (f0994, f1035). At the end of the beat the RDP end-entity card, labelled 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab / Remote Desktop Authentication', sits at the Root CA's press on the gold plinth (f1077). Visually, the root issued the end-entity certificate (AR-02 violated), and the root operates in the present (B-05.1 constraint).

The card and its translucent CA 1 copy lock in beside the anchored key container, and the key does not move. But the card has just come from the root's press (B-04.4 f1077 to B-04.5 f1084), so the viewer sees a root-issued certificate being installed.
A gold vault on a cable-free plinth carries a static ring seal, and its press and module are dark in this beat. (Its press was already used in B-04.2 to B-04.4; see K2-02.)

A desaturated flashback marked 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony'. Issuing CA 1's own CA request is carried to the root's removable-media slot, under the caption 'The Root CA signs the issuing CA certificate'. The tag and the CA=true band are tiny in f1320 (K2-06).

A trust link grows from the root to the certificate on CA 1's crown, and the root stays cable-free. The caption 'The Root CA is the trust anchor' applies to the root only. The link is white rather than gold-to-cyan (K2-07). The beat's own constraint, 'no end-entity request ever travels to the root', is contradicted by B-04.2.

A new amber pulse runs client to server, and two cyan cards (the server certificate and the CA 1 copy) arrive at CLIENT01. The key stays in the server. The handshake impression is not clearly visible at this tier, and the cards are already beside the client at f1504 (K2-09).
The cards dock upward (server certificate, then CA 1) into a gold root already in its cradle, with 'Installed earlier by policy'. Nothing travels from AD.
The tags read 'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it' and 'Fetching never creates trust'. Nothing is fetched.
Six distinct checks appear, including 'Name matches rdp01.1sn0s.lab' and 'EKU permits RDP'. Revocation is shown pending (amber tick).
Two amber CRL scrolls dock to the two non-root cards and none to the gold root. 'OCSP if deployed' sits on the client's check list, not on the kiosk.
The channel turns green only after all six ticks, and the session window opens. Caption: 'Trusted RDP connection established'.
The camera glides to WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab with its WebServer-TLS badge. An amber dot lingers at the RDP server (K2-08).
A local key pair forms, the private key is locked in its container, and the capsule is sealed by a beam. No key moves.
CA 1 is tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here'. CA 2 shows the four eligibility tags, and a violet route lights to CA 2 only. The capsule stays at WEB01.
The capsule follows the violet route into the Issuing CA 2 vault only. It does not go near the root, which is the correct counterpart to the faulty B-04.2.
The capsule is inside CA 2 while the compressed checks run. Check 1 and the 'Name supplied in request' note are occluded or overprinted (K2-05).
CA 2 stamps a card reading 'portal.1sn0s.lab / Server Authentication' inside its own vault (f2633). The card returns to WEB01 beside the anchored key. The root's press is untouched.
A link from the root reveals CA 2's existing crown certificate. The root's press and module stay dark, and the root has no cables. The link is white, not gold (K2-07).
The violet cards dock into the same gold root, the compressed ticks (name, EKU, validity, revocation) resolve, and the channel turns green.
Hero topology: one root on top, CA 1 and CA 2 below, cyan and violet paths down to the servers. The root has no cables. Caption: 'Different issuing paths. One trusted root.'
The title card 'Certificate Flow — From request to trust', then a clean fade to black.

findings.evidence: After B-04.1 lights the cyan route to Issuing CA 1, the white RDP request capsule floats up past the '1SN0S Root CA' label (f0840). It comes to rest in the head of the Root CA's press on the gold plinth (f0867), and is still there at the start of B-04.3 (f0874). Issuing CA 1's vault stays empty of any capsule. The model dump says E-04.2a goes from RDP_SERVER to ISSUING_CA1, so the render contradicts the model.
findings.why: An end-entity request reaches the offline Root CA. AR-02 says the root never receives an end-entity request, and AR-01 says the root has no live connection. The film's own B-05.3 constraint, 'No end-entity request ever travels to the root', is then false. Under the spec, any Root CA violation is a BLOCKER.
findings.direction: The capsule must travel only along the lit cyan route and end inside the Issuing CA 1 vault, at CA 1's press. It must never come near the root plinth. The rendered path must match E-04.2a.

findings.evidence: Issuing CA 1's press never stamps anything in B-04.4 (f0994, f1035). At f1077 the RDP end-entity card ('rdp01.1sn0s.lab / Remote Desktop Authentication') appears at the Root CA's press on the gold plinth. In the next beat (f1084) the card is inside CA 1, about to travel to rdp01.
findings.why: On screen, the Root CA issues an end-entity certificate, and its press operates in the present. This contradicts AR-02 (the root signs only issuing CA certificates and its CRL) and the B-05.1 constraint that the root performs no signing in the present. It also regresses PKI-S0R1-03.
findings.direction: The request must be consumed at Issuing CA 1's own press, driven by CA 1's sealed key module. The card must be stamped there. The root's press and module must stay dark and still for the whole present-tense film.

findings.evidence: The discovery step lights a route to Issuing CA 1 only (f0807). The capsule then ignores that route and is delivered to the Root CA (f0840, f0867). The root is a standalone CA that publishes no templates (AR-04).
findings.why: The request is sent to a CA that does not publish RDPAuth, and the visible discovery result is ignored. This contradicts F-05: the client never sends to a CA that does not publish the template, and never picks a CA arbitrarily.
findings.direction: After the lookup, the request goes only to the eligible CA that was discovered, along the lit route.

findings.evidence: The caption 'Issuing CA 1 verifies, then signs' first appears over the Root CA's press holding the capsule (f0874). The four check ticks then resolve inside Issuing CA 1 while no request capsule is in that vault (f0930, f0987).
findings.why: The checks are shown evaluating a request that is not at the CA, and the caption naming CA 1 is placed on the root. Viewers cannot tell which CA evaluates and signs. This is misleading even apart from the root violation.
findings.direction: Keep the capsule visibly inside Issuing CA 1, at its press, while each of the four checks resolves. Put the caption only on CA 1 shots.

findings.evidence: The '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' / '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' name plate sits directly over check 1, 'Requester authenticated': only 'enticat' is visible, at f0930, f0987, f0994, f2513 and f2562. In B-08.1 the note 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is printed on top of 'Request meets template policy', so both are unreadable (f2513, f2562).
findings.why: F-06 requires four distinct checks, and the first, authenticating the requester, is never readable. B-08.1's required restriction note (the F-07 rationale) is illegible, so the viewer sees three checks and an unexplained overlap.
findings.direction: Move the CA name plate clear of the check list. Give the restriction note its own line, so all four checks and the note can be read during their beats.

findings.evidence: When the CA request reaches the root's removable-media slot (f1320), its tag 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' is a few pixels high and the cyan CA=true band cannot be made out. The tag is readable only earlier, over CA 1 (strip frame 2).
findings.why: The tag and band are what separate this request from the RDP request (PKI-S0R1-02). Here that matters more, because the film has just shown the RDP request going to the root.
findings.direction: Keep the tag readable, and the CA=true band visible, while the capsule is at the root.

findings.evidence: The issuer links from the root to the CA crowns render near-white, not gold-to-cyan or gold.
findings.why: Spec B-05.3 and B-08.3 call for gold links. The trust colour language ties each issuer relationship to the trust anchor.
findings.direction: Render the links using the gold role token, blending to the issuing CA's colour.

findings.evidence: An amber dot stays on the RDP server end of the channel after the channel has turned green.
findings.why: Amber means a pending connection. A leftover amber marker on a validated connection muddles the 'trusted' state.
findings.direction: Retire or recolour the pulse marker when the channel turns green.

findings.evidence: At f1504, three frames into B-06.1, two cyan cards labelled rdp01.1sn0s.lab already hover beside CLIENT01. The handshake-proof impression is not distinguishable at this tier.
findings.why: The causal order must be: pulse arrives, server presents, proof travels and is verified. If the cards are at the client before the presentation, that order is weakened (PKI-S0R2-02, PKI-S0R2-03).
findings.direction: Make sure the cards and the impression are visibly at the server and travel to the client only after the pulse arrives. Make the impression readable.

findings.evidence: Inside the flashback, Issuing CA 1's vault still shows the present-tense RDP check list ('Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted', 'Request meets templ...').
findings.why: Showing the setup ceremony together with the later end-entity checks blurs the eras. Combined with PKI-S1K2-01, it suggests the RDP evaluation and the root ceremony are linked.
findings.direction: Hide present-tense check labels during the flashback.

findings.evidence: At f0765 the capsule appears at the foot of the 1SN0S.LAB pillar, away from the server's outbound port. No separate steel-blue query pulse to AD and back can be seen in any B-04.1 frame.
findings.why: Viewers may read the capsule as going to AD. The spec says the capsule is held at the outbound port while a separate query pulse goes to AD and back.
findings.direction: Keep the capsule visibly attached to the server's port, and make the steel-blue query pulse visible.
